content: Asymptomatic Bacteriuria Definitions: In women, asymptomatic bacteriuria is defined as the presence of the same bacterial strain in two consecutive voided urine specimens, each with a bacterial count of ≥ 10⁵ colony-forming units (CFU) per milliliter. In men, it is defined as a single, clean-catch voided urine specimen with one bacterial species isolated in a quantitative count of ≥ 10⁵ CFU/mL. For catheterized urine specimens, it is defined as a single catheterized urine specimen with one bacterial species isolated in a quantitative count of ≥ 10² CFU/mL. Causative Pathogens: Common pathogens include Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, coagulase-negative staphylococci, Enterococcus, Group B streptococci, Gardnerella vaginalis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Proteus mirabilis, Providencia stuartii, and Morganella morganii. The latter three are more common in patients with long-term urologic devices. Empiric Antimicrobial Therapy: Treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria is not recommended for the following groups: Premenopausal, nonpregnant women. Diabetic women. Older adults residing in the community. Elderly individuals in long-term care facilities. Patients with spinal cord injuries. Patients with indwelling urethral catheters while the catheter remains in place. Specific Considerations: Men: Screening or treatment for asymptomatic bacteriuria is not recommended. Premenopausal, nonpregnant women: Screening or treatment is not indicated. Pregnant women: Treatment is recommended with one of the following regimens: 1. Nitrofurantoin 100 mg orally twice daily for 3–5 days (avoid in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency). 2. Amoxicillin 500 mg orally three times daily for 3–5 days. 3. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 500 mg orally twice daily for 3–5 days. 4. Cephalexin 500 mg orally three times daily for 3–5 days. 5. Fosfomycin 3 g as a single dose. 6. Trimethoprim orally twice daily for 3–5 days (only after the first trimester). Diabetic women: Screening or treatment is not recommended. Older adults in the community: Screening or treatment is not recommended. Institutionalized elderly individuals: Screening or treatment is not recommended. Patients with spinal cord injuries: Screening or treatment is not recommended. Patients with indwelling urethral catheters: Screening or treatment is not recommended while the catheter remains in place. Urologic interventions: Screening or treatment is recommended before transurethral resection of the prostate. Scabies Preferred Regimen: Permethrin cream (5%) applied to all areas of the body from the neck down and washed off after 8–14 hours. Alternatively, Ivermectin 200 µg/kg orally, repeated in 2 weeks. Alternative Regimens: Lindane (1%) solution or gel. Imiquimod 5% cream. Sinecatechins 15% ointment. Provider-Administered Treatments: Cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen or cryoprobe, repeated every 1–2 weeks. Podophyllin resin 10–25% in a compound tincture of benzoin. Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) or bichloroacetic acid (BCA) 80–90%. Surgical removal via tangential scissor excision, shave excision, curettage, or electrosurgery. Trichomoniasis (Trichomonas vaginalis) Preferred Regimen: Metronidazole 2 g orally in a single dose. Tinidazole 2 g orally in a single dose. Alternative Regimen: Metronidazole 500 mg orally twice daily for 7 days. Pregnancy Considerations: Metronidazole 2 g orally in a single dose can be administered at any stage of pregnancy. Breastfeeding should be withheld during treatment and for 12–24 hours after the last dose to minimize infant exposure. Acute Uncomplicated Cystitis Preferred Regimens: 1. Nitrofurantoin monohydrate/macrocrystals 100 mg orally twice daily for 5 days (avoid if early pyelonephritis is suspected). 2. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 160/800 mg (one double-strength tablet) orally twice daily for 3 days (avoid if resistance prevalence exceeds 20% or if used for UTI in the previous 3 months). 3. Fosfomycin trometamol 3 g as a single dose (lower efficacy; avoid if early pyelonephritis is suspected). 4. Pivmecillinam 400 mg orally twice daily for 5 days (lower efficacy; avoid if early pyelonephritis is suspected). Alternative Regimens: Fluoroquinolones (e.g., ofloxacin, ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin) for 3 days. β-lactam agents (e.g., amoxicillin-clavulanate, cefdinir, cefaclor, cefpodoxime-proxetil) for 3–7 days. Genital Herpes First Episode: Acyclovir 400 mg orally three times daily for 7–10 days. Famciclovir 250 mg orally three times daily for 7–10 days. Valacyclovir 1 g orally twice daily for 7–10 days. Recurrent Episodes: Suppressive therapy: Acyclovir 400 mg orally twice daily, Famciclovir 250 mg orally twice daily, or Valacyclovir 500–1000 mg orally once daily. Episodic therapy: Acyclovir 400 mg orally three times daily for 5 days or Valacyclovir 500 mg orally twice daily for 3 days. Severe Disease: Acyclovir 5–10 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 2–7 days, followed by oral antiviral therapy to complete at least 10 days of total treatment.
